Complementary information — The documents provide different cost figures for various valve types, procedures, countries, and time periods, which together give a fuller picture without contradiction.

The evidence clusters by scope: d2, d4, d6, and d7 give U.S. average costs for specific procedures (aortic valve replacement, TAVR/SAVR) ranging from ~$59,000 to $170,000 [d2, d4, d6, d7]. d3 and d5 provide costs for mitral valve repair/replacement ($11,606–$45,072 and ~$30,720) [d3, d5]. d8 gives valve device costs ($5,000–$10,000), and d1 and d9 discuss cost components and factors like insurance and follow-up care [d1, d8, d9]. These are complementary facets of the total cost.

The final answer will synthesize these complementary figures, noting that costs vary widely by procedure, valve type, location, and included expenses. No single document gives a universal cost, but together they illustrate the range and key determinants.

The cost of heart valve surgery varies significantly depending on the procedure, valve type, country, and what costs are included. In the United States, average costs for aortic valve replacement surgery are about $59,000 [d2], while a 2021 average for a heart valve replacement procedure was $170,000 [d6]. Specific procedure costs include $59,743 for surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) and $64,395 for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) over six months [d4]. For mitral valve surgery, mean costs are around $30,720 for repair and $28,717 for replacement [d5], though other data show costs from $11,606 to $45,072 [d3]. The cost also includes surgeon fees, hospital fees, medications, and follow-up care [d1], and can be influenced by patient age, comorbidities, and complications [d9]. The valve device itself may cost between $5,000 and $10,000 [d8].
